# StripesTestIncreasingWidth

PCell declaration for optical lithography test stripes.

**Source:** KQC (KQCircuits). **Category:** test_structure. **Module:** `kqcircuits.test_structures.stripes_test_increasing_width`.

:::{note}
Canonical cell of an alias group. Aliases: [`StripesTest`](StripesTest.md).
:::

See also the [catalog](../CATALOG.md) and the [duplicates decisions](../DUPLICATES.md).

## Pins

![Pins of StripesTestIncreasingWidth](../../images/components/StripesTestIncreasingWidth.png)

Pin image (default parameters). Light = metal, dark = etched gap, colours = junction layers. A red dot and arrow is a pin and its direction (out of the cell); the red bar is the CPW width a + 2 b. Blue dot = a pin without direction. Units: µm.

No pins: this cell has no ports. Place it with `at=` / `rot=`.

## Parameters

| name | default | unit | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | `10` | μm | Width of center conductor |
| `b` | `6` | μm | Width of gap |
| `r` | `100` | μm | Turn radius |
| `min_stripe_width` | `1` | μm | Beginning width of the stripe sequence |
| `stripe_length` | `100` | μm | Length of the stripes |
| `stripe_spacing` | `1` | μm | Spacing between the stripes |
| `num_stripes` | `20` | – | Number of stripes |
| `stripe_step` | `1` | μm | Stripe widening increment in the stripe sequence |

Electrically relevant parameters (sizes, gaps, junction, ports) come first, the rest follows.

## LOM model

none (a LOM build gives each pin its own bare node, without elements).

## How to use

In Python:

```python
from quantcore_circuits.designer import Designer

d = Designer("demo", box=(0, 0, 7500, 7500))
d.add("U1", "StripesTestIncreasingWidth", at=(3750, 3750), a=10)   # parameters: see the table above
# no directed pin: place it with at= / rot=, or snap it with snap= / to=
```

Pin names go into `d.route(...)` as `INSTANCE.pin`, and into `snap=` / `to=` when placing. From the shell: `qcc components StripesTestIncreasingWidth` lists the pins; add `--schema` for the parameters.

In KLayout: Quantcore panel ▸ Components ▸ double-click the cell, then click on the layout to place it. Rotate and mirror before the click; use Connect on two pins to route.
